subject: Best way to fix or free specific parameters in a matrix?

messages.author: cf47bbe63da1f3ae
messages.subject: Best way to fix or free specific parameters in a matrix?
parts:
I currently have a package to allow a relatively easy specification of dynamic factor models, for both discrete and continuous time. I'd like for the model specification function I've written to be able to then fit using STAN, as well as the SEM software I currently use, OpenMx.  I've set the basics of the models up in STAN, but I really need to find a way to have certain parameters in the matrices I'm inputting become free or fixed.  Something like the below specification would be perfect, where I import a matrix of values, MANIFESTVAR, then specify that certain of those are free. This would need some R code in the middle of course to determine which parameters, but this is ok.

data {
cov_matrix[nmanifest] MANIFESTVAR;
}
parameters {
real <lower=0> MANIFESTVAR[2,2];
}

Obviously, such a specification doesn't work - but is there an approach that may be equivalent?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Best way to fix or free specific parameters in a matrix?
parts:
> On May 12, 2015, at 8:33 AM, Charles Driver <cdriv...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I currently have a package to allow a relatively easy specification of dynamic factor models, for both discrete and continuous time. I'd like for the model specification function I've written to be able to then fit using STAN, as well as the SEM software I currently use, OpenMx. I've set the basics of the models up in STAN, but I really need to find a way to have certain parameters in the matrices I'm inputting become free or fixed. Something like the below specification would be perfect, where I import a matrix of values, MANIFESTVAR, then specify that certain of those are free. This would need some R code in the middle of course to determine which parameters, but this is ok.
>
> data {
> cov_matrix[nmanifest] MANIFESTVAR;
> }
> parameters {
> real <lower=0> MANIFESTVAR[2,2];
> }
>
> Obviously, such a specification doesn't work - but is there an approach that may be equivalent?

I'm not sure what your intention was with that sketch. Was it that
all of cov_matrix is specified as data other than element at index (2,2),
which is unknown with a lower-bound of 0?

Check out the missing data chapter for an example of how to handle
this kind of thing (the known values are data and the unknown values
are like "missing data"). You can do this with some just having constraints,
too.

It's tricky with covariance matrices, though, because you need
to make sure the result is positive definite or you'll run into
trouble sampling.

- Bob
